exercises.prompt: You are given roster, an array of Pokémon records, each an object { name, type, attack, defense } — for example { name: 'charmander', type: 'fire', attack: 52, defense: 43 }. Implement countByType(roster) so it returns an object mapping each type to how many records have it — { type: count }. countByType(roster) is {fire: 4, water: 4, grass: 3, electric: 2, rock: 2}. An empty roster returns an empty object {}.
exercises.fixture:
const roster = [
  { name: 'charmander', type: 'fire', attack: 52, defense: 43 },
  { name: 'charizard', type: 'fire', attack: 84, defense: 78 },
  { name: 'vulpix', type: 'fire', attack: 41, defense: 40 },
  { name: 'growlithe', type: 'fire', attack: 70, defense: 45 },
  { name: 'squirtle', type: 'water', attack: 48, defense: 65 },
  { name: 'blastoise', type: 'water', attack: 83, defense: 100 },
  { name: 'psyduck', type: 'water', attack: 52, defense: 48 },
  { name: 'staryu', type: 'water', attack: 45, defense: 55 },
  { name: 'bulbasaur', type: 'grass', attack: 49, defense: 49 },
  { name: 'oddish', type: 'grass', attack: 50, defense: 55 },
  { name: 'bellsprout', type: 'grass', attack: 75, defense: 35 },

tests.expr: countByType([{ name: 'a', type: 'ghost', attack: 1, defense: 1 }, { name: 'b', type: 'ghost', attack: 2, defense: 2 }])

hints: This is a frequency tally, but the value you count is each record's type field rather than the record itself.
Walk the records and bump the bucket for p.type: counts[p.type] = (counts[p.type] || 0) + 1.
Loop the roster updating counts[p.type] = (counts[p.type] || 0) + 1, then return counts — || 0 seeds the first record of each type, and an empty roster never enters the loop so you return {}.

A type no record has, or an empty roster, returns 0.

hints: Two steps: narrow to the records of the requested type, then add up their attack values.
filter(p => p.type === type) keeps the matching records; reduce with a 0 seed sums a field: (sum, p) => sum + p.attack.
return roster.filter(p => p.type === type).reduce((sum, p) => sum + p.attack, 0) — the 0 seed is both the running total and the answer when no record matches.

hints: Track the best record seen so far for each type as you walk the roster — one running leader per bucket.
For each record, replace the type's leader only when p.attack is strictly greater than the stored one, then read each leader's .name at the end.
Use if (!(p.type in best) || p.attack > best[p.type].attack) best[p.type] = p — strictly > keeps the earlier record on a tie, matching the fourth test where 'first' wins over 'second'.

hints: You need two tallies per type as you walk the roster: a running sum of attack and a running count of records.
Accumulate sums[p.type] and counts[p.type] together, then in a second pass divide and round: Math.round(sums[type] / counts[type]).
The rock average is (80 + 45) / 2 = 62.5, which Math.round turns into 63 — flooring or truncating would wrongly give 62, so round rather than cut.

Records that tie on attack keep their original roster order relative to each other. topByAttack(roster, 3) is ['charizard', 'blastoise', 'geodude']. If n is 0 the result is empty; if n exceeds the roster length, return every name in sorted order. Do not modify the roster.

hints: Sort a copy of the roster by attack descending, then take the first n and pull each name out.
[...roster].sort((a, b) => b.attack - a.attack) orders strongest-first without touching the original; slice(0, n) is safe when n is 0 or larger than the array.
return [...roster].sort((a, b) => b.attack - a.attack).slice(0, n).map(p => p.name) — sort is stable, so charmander (attack 52) stays ahead of psyduck (also 52) as the eighth-place test checks.

exercises.prompt: You are given roster, an array of Pokémon records of shape { name, type, attack, defense }. Implement namesByTypeAbove(roster, minAttack) so it returns an object mapping each type to an array of the names of its records whose attack is greater than or equal to minAttack, each array in roster order — { type: [name, ...] }. A type with no qualifying record must be absent from the result entirely, not mapped to an empty array. namesByTypeAbove(roster, 50) is {fire: ['charmander', 'charizard', 'growlithe'], water: ['blastoise', 'psyduck'], grass: ['oddish', 'bellsprout'], electric: ['pikachu'], rock: ['geodude']}. hints: Group and filter in the same pass: only a record that clears minAttack may create or join a bucket.
Create each array lazily with (groups[p.type] ||= []).push(p.name), so a type appears only once a qualifying record shows up.

Loop with if (p.attack >= minAttack) (groups[p.type] ||= []).push(p.name) and return groups — >= keeps oddish at exactly 50, and grass and electric are simply missing at minAttack 80 because nothing ever seeded them.
